title: Adjournment debate on access to school co-curricular activities
what_it_is: An adjournment motion in which Mr Kenneth Tiong spoke on access to co-curricular activities and proposed reforms, followed by a response from Senior Minister of State for Education David Neo, before Parliament adjourned.
why_it_matters: The record sets out proposals to widen access to CCAs, including extending the primary school no-trial pilot to secondary schools, allowing students to change CCAs without LEAPS penalty, and expanding cross-school programmes. The Senior Minister of State said MOE and MCCY are working to share facilities and provide professional coaching across schools, that students from lower-income families can tap the MOE Opportunity Fund for CCA expenses, and that strengthening access to CCAs is a key priority. He said more details will be announced at MCCY’s Committee of Supply debates later.

key_points.point: The Leader of the House moved that Parliament do now adjourn.
key_points.speaker: The Leader of the House (Ms Indranee Rajah)
key_points.quote: That Parliament do now adjourn.

key_points.point: Mr Kenneth Tiong said he wished to discuss the co-curricular activities system.
key_points.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
key_points.quote: I wish to discuss our co-curricular activities (CCA) system.

key_points.point: He said each January Secondary 1 students submit a ranked list of CCA preferences.
key_points.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
key_points.quote: Each January, Secondary 1 students submit a ranked list of CCA preferences.

key_points.point: He said schools conduct trials and auditions for popular CCAs, sports and performing arts.
key_points.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
key_points.quote: For popular CCAs, sports, performing arts, schools conduct trials and auditions.

key_points.point: He said students who do not pass are asked to remove that CCA from their choices.
key_points.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
key_points.quote: Students who do not pass are asked to remove that CCA from their choices.

key_points.point: He said CCA is compulsory and students must participate for four to five years.
key_points.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
key_points.quote: CCA is compulsory. Students must participate for four to five years.

key_points.point: He said under LEAPS 2.0 participation is graded and grades translate into bonus points for post-secondary admission.
key_points.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
key_points.quote: Under LEAPS 2.0, that participation is graded and those grades translate into bonus points for post-secondary admission.

key_points.point: He said the Ministry piloted removal of CCA selection trials across eight primary schools in 2020.
key_points.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
key_points.quote: In 2020, the Ministry piloted the removal of CCA selection trials across eight primary schools.

key_points.point: He said about two-thirds of primary schools today operate without trials.
key_points.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
key_points.quote: Today, about two-thirds of primary schools operate without trials.

key_points.point: He proposed extending the primary school pilot to secondary schools.
key_points.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
key_points.quote: Extend the primary school pilot to secondary schools.

key_points.point: He proposed that selection trials sort students into a competitive squad and a developmental programme, not into participants and the excluded.
key_points.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
key_points.quote: Where a CCA conducts selection trials, these trials should sort students into a competitive squad and a developmental programme – not into participants and the excluded.

key_points.point: He proposed every student should be able to join at least one of their top CCA choices.
key_points.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
key_points.quote: Every student should be able to join at least one of their top CCA choices.

key_points.point: He proposed allowing students to change CCAs at the end of Secondary 1 or Secondary 2 without LEAPS penalty.
key_points.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
key_points.quote: I propose that students be allowed to change CCAs at the end of Secondary 1 or end of Secondary 2 without penalty under LEAPS.

key_points.point: He said the SP-CCA programme today serves 232 students from 86 schools across four sports.
key_points.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
key_points.quote: The Strategic Partnership CCA (SP-CCA) programme today serves 232 students from 86 schools across four sports.

key_points.point: He proposed doubling SP-CCA from four sports to eight sports within two years.
key_points.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
key_points.quote: One, to double SP-CCA from four sports to eight sports within two years.

key_points.point: He proposed publishing a sport-by-sport availability map showing which sports are offered at which schools.
key_points.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
key_points.quote: Two, publish a sport-by-sport availability map, showing which sports are offered at which schools, so that gaps are visible and planning is data-driven.

key_points.point: He proposed publishing a five-year SP-CCA expansion roadmap and inviting schools to form voluntary geographic clusters of four to six schools.
key_points.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
key_points.quote: Three, publish a five-year SP-CCA expansion roadmap with clear targets and invite schools to form voluntary geographic clusters of four to six schools, pooling CCA offerings, so students can cross-attend.

key_points.point: He asked whether students in structured external programmes could be eligible for CCA recognition, subject to school verification.
key_points.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
key_points.quote: Could students participating in a structured external programme – ActiveSG, a National Sports Association, or a registered academy – be eligible for CCA recognition, subject to verification by the school?

key_points.point: He asked whether the Junior Sports Academy intake could be doubled or tripled given demand exceeds supply.
key_points.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
key_points.quote: And at primary level, could we double or triple the Junior Sports Academy intake – this fully Ministry of Education (MOE)-funded, non-competitive, multi-sport programme – given demand already exceeds supply?

key_points.point: He proposed CoachSG create a new NROC tier for an Assistant Coach or Recreational Coach credential.
key_points.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
key_points.quote: I propose that CoachSG create a new NROC tier – an Assistant Coach or Recreational Coach credential, completable in eight to 16 hours at nominal cost, covering maybe Safe Sport, first-aid, values-based coaching and inclusive session design.

key_points.point: He proposed reviewing the LEAPS 2.0 Achievement domain.
key_points.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
key_points.quote: Review the LEAPS 2.0 Achievement domain.

key_points.point: He proposed requiring MOE to collect and publish socio-economic data on DSA applications and outcomes.
key_points.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
key_points.quote: And require MOE to collect and publish socio-economic data on DSA applications and outcomes – household income quartile, participation in paid preparatory programmes.

key_points.point: Mr David Neo said the CCA landscape is not perfect and challenges remain.
key_points.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Mr David Neo)
key_points.quote: we acknowledge the CCA landscape is not perfect and challenges remain

key_points.point: He said the Government will continue to review and improve.
key_points.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Mr David Neo)
key_points.quote: Let me assure the House that we will continue to review and to improve.

key_points.point: He said they are working to further widen access for students to a greater diversity of CCAs.
key_points.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Mr David Neo)
key_points.quote: On access, and selecting one's favourite CCAs, we are working to further widen access for students to a greater diversity of CCAs.

key_points.point: He said MOE and MCCY, including Sport Singapore and the National Arts Council, are working together to share facilities and provide professional coaching across schools.
key_points.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Mr David Neo)
key_points.quote: MOE and the Ministry of Culture, Community and Youth (MCCY), in particular Sport Singapore and the National Arts Council, are working together to share facilities and provide professional coaching across schools.

key_points.point: He said SP-CCA enables secondary school students to pursue activities beyond what their individual schools offer.
key_points.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Mr David Neo)
key_points.quote: Members may also be aware of the SP-CCA, the Member mentioned it as well, which enables secondary school students to pursue activities beyond what their individual schools offer.

key_points.point: He said CCAs can be expanded to more students and more schools so students can choose and participate in their choice CCA.
key_points.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Mr David Neo)
key_points.quote: I thank the Member for agreeing that we can expand these CCAs to more students and more schools so that students can get to choose and participate in their choice CCA.

key_points.point: He said he will announce more details at MCCY’s Committee of Supply debates later.
key_points.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Mr David Neo)
key_points.quote: I will announce more details at the MCCY’s Committee of Supply (COS) debates later.

key_points.point: He said students from disadvantaged backgrounds will continue to be supported.
key_points.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Mr David Neo)
key_points.quote: We will continue to ensure that students from disadvantaged backgrounds are supported.

key_points.point: He said students from lower-income families can tap the MOE Opportunity Fund for learning experiences and additional CCA expenses.
key_points.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Mr David Neo)
key_points.quote: Minister Desmond Lee, in his COS speech this morning, has said that students from lower-income families can tap on the MOE Opportunity Fund for learning experiences and any additional CCA expenses.

key_points.point: He said they will explore how to increase access to the Junior Sports Academy programme.
key_points.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Mr David Neo)
key_points.quote: And yes, we will explore how to increase access to the Junior Sports Academy programme as well.

key_points.point: He said coaches will continue to be required to possess NROC certification.
key_points.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Mr David Neo)
key_points.quote: I think you will have to continue to require that our coaches do possess NROC certification.

key_points.point: He said strengthening access to CCAs is a key priority, including allowing more students their first choice and strengthening access for disadvantaged students.
key_points.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Education (Mr David Neo)
key_points.quote: And as part of this, strengthening access to CCAs for students is a key priority, including allowing more of them their first choice and strengthening access for students from disadvantaged backgrounds.

key_points.point: Parliament adjourned at 9.07 pm.
key_points.speaker: Mr Speaker
key_points.quote: Adjourned accordingly at 9.07 pm.

what_happens_next: Mr David Neo said he will announce more details at the MCCY’s Committee of Supply debates later; Parliament adjourned at 9.07 pm.
